subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should the implementation use a per-kind capability while keeping Telegram's default top-level placement as current?
rationale: Current main already has core binding primitives, but the remaining behavior affects visible Telegram topic creation, plugin capability/API shape, and session/message routing defaults; automation should not choose that product boundary.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the primary design input, resolve conflicts and findings, and require live Telegram proof on the final head before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the visibility and API model for child topics.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs as not planned if maintainers decide internal subagent work should never create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the primary design input, resolve conflicts and findings, and require live Telegram proof on the final head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice sits on the core thread-binding refactor and channel capability policy he most directly owns in current history.
